requirements.requirement: Serve a package repository from local storage on node1
requirements.summary: createrepo_c installed, tree RPM downloaded into /srv/local-repo, repodata generated with createrepo_c, and a python3 http.server exposed the directory on NODE_IP:8080 (curl returned 200 for repomd.xml). A local-storage.repo pointing at that URL was added and appeared in dnf repolist.

requirements.requirement: Usual remote repositories made unreachable before the install
requirements.summary: cdn.redhat.com was redirected to loopback via /etc/hosts (subsequent curl to it returned exit 7 / status 000), and both RHEL CDN repos were disabled, leaving dnf repolist showing only local-storage enabled.

requirements.requirement: Package installed successfully from the local repo while remote repos were unreachable
requirements.summary: dnf install -y tree completed successfully sourcing only from the 'local-storage' repo; tree --version confirmed the binary works, and cdn.redhat.com was independently reconfirmed unreachable (status 000) during/around the install.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task are directly and coherently satisfied: a local RPM repository was built from local storage and served over HTTP, the remote CDN repos were made genuinely unreachable (verified via curl failures and repolist), and the tree package was installed and verified functional using only the local repo while the remote repos were unreachable. The executor also restored remote connectivity and repo configuration afterward and cleanly executed the independent node-restart evidence protocol: a healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id, tree installed, repo HTTP 200) was captured, systemctl reboot was acknowledged, the node was observed unreachable and then recovered, boot_id changed post-restart (matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots exactly), and the installed package plus repo files/config were confirmed intact after reboot.
limitations: The post-restart verification (cmd-a2cf9916a17040b7) confirmed the repo files and repo configuration persisted, but did not re-curl the HTTP endpoint to confirm the python http.server was still serving after reboot; since it was launched as an ad hoc background process rather than a systemd service, it likely did not survive the reboot. This does not affect the task's material outcomes since persistence of the HTTP service across reboot was not part of the task contract, but it is a gap in the restart evidence for that specific component.
Evidence is limited to captured command transcripts; live system state beyond these snapshots (e.g., current state of the http.server process) could not be independently verified.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor's mutations (installing createrepo_c, downloading/building the local repo, starting the HTTP server, adding the repo file, editing /etc/hosts, disabling/re-enabling CDN repos, installing tree, and the restart) each map directly to a task requirement, a necessary prerequisite for simulating unreachability, or cleanup/restoration. The disruptive /etc/hosts entry and disabled repos were fully reverted (cmd-d2d0d6beba3949f9) and connectivity/re-enablement was verified (cmd-9119252d095b47c7, cmd-70f0c5c689f846ad). No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found; failed-services and listening-socket snapshots show no new failures or exposure introduced by the executor (only expected sshd/chronyd pid changes from reboot). Minor residue: leftover /tmp/httpd.log, /tmp/httpd.pid, /tmp/reboot.log and the running python http.server/local-storage.repo are retained, but these are the intended deliverable artifacts of the task (a served local repo) rather than unwanted leftovers, so this is not penalized. The restart used a backgrounded nohup+disown pattern to return the acknowledgement before disconnect, which is a reasonable low-risk technique.
